title: boomtime · Service & Infra
description: Consolidated Ops view (replaces boomtime-keda-scaling + boomtime-worker-queue). First-party Prometheus RED (incoming router + outbound clients), Go/process runtime, DB & Redis pools, cache hit-rate, the concurrency + HTTP rate limiters, and the KEDA/RabbitMQ image-job autoscaling. Scrape: boomtime ServiceMonitor /metrics (server role only).

panels.title: Job-limiter headroom (in-flight / max) by kind
panels.description: This pod's in-flight slots / configured fleet-wide cap. Near 1 = saturated.

panels.description: acquired = throughput, atlimit = back-pressure, error = broker failure.

panels.title: Memory (heap in-use / RSS)
panels.description: Go heap in-use and process resident set size.

panels.title: CPU / open FDs
panels.description: Process CPU (cores) and open file descriptors.

panels.title: DB pool — connections vs max
panels.description: pgx pool occupancy. total pinned near max = pool exhaustion risk.

panels.title: DB pool — acquire pressure
panels.description: Acquire rate, empty-pool acquires (had to wait), and mean blocking time per acquire.

panels.title: Redis pool — hit ratio by purpose

targets.expr: sum by (purpose) (rate(redis_pool_hits_total{namespace="boomtime"}[$__rate_interval])) / clamp_min(sum by (purpose) (rate(redis_pool_hits_total{namespace="boomtime"}[$__rate_interval])) + sum by (purpose) (rate(redis_pool_misses_total{namespace="boomtime"}[$__rate_interval])), 1e-9)

panels.description: Connection-pool hit ratio (free conn reused vs new dial) per client purpose.

panels.title: Redis pool — conns & timeouts
panels.description: Redis/Dragonfly pool size and wait-timeout rate per purpose.

panels.title: Cache hit rate by cache
panels.description: In-memory TTL cache effectiveness per named cache.

panels.title: Queue depth (ready)
panels.description: Messages published but not yet picked up by a consumer. Sustained >0 with 0 consumers means the worker is scaled to zero (KEDA cold start) or down.

panels.title: Consumers
panels.description: AMQP consumers currently subscribed — should track the worker replica count 1:1 (concurrency=1 per consumer prefetch-qos slot per worker pod, see BOOM_LABEL_IMAGE_CONCURRENCY).

panels.title: boomtime-worker replicas
panels.description: Current replica count of the Deployment KEDA scales (min 0 / max 4, see keda-scaledobject.yaml).

panels.title: Unacked (in-flight)
panels.description: Delivered to a worker but not yet ack'd — a job actively regenerating (or stuck mid-crash awaiting redelivery).

panels.title: boomtime-worker replicas (KEDA scaling activity)
panels.description: The observable effect of the ScaledObject reacting to queue depth — should rise shortly after a burst of enqueues and fall back to 0 after the cooldownPeriod (120s) once the queue drains.

panels.title: Publish / deliver rate
panels.description: Enqueue rate (server publishes) vs. delivery rate (worker consumes). A widening gap between the two means the queue is growing faster than the worker(s) can drain it.

panels.title: Scaler active (queue has work)
panels.description: keda_scaler_active = 1 when the trigger has messages → KEDA scales the worker up from 0.

panels.title: Trigger metric value (queue depth KEDA reads) vs threshold
panels.description: keda_scaler_metrics_value is the RabbitMQ queue length the scaler polls; the ScaledObject scales on it (target 5).

panels.title: All ScaledObjects — active state (cluster)
panels.description: Every KEDA ScaledObject's active flag across the cluster — quick health glance.
